claim: Human RT in mental rotation and image scanning rises linearly with angle or distance (Shepard-Metzler, Kosslyn island map). Exact slopes are recalled in a/b, not re-read; the pattern is agreed by both sides. Gap-search: Shepard-Metzler 1971 and Kosslyn 1978 abstracts confirm the linear pattern; the 1978 abstract adds that distance had no effect when subjects were not told to use images. Scanning splits into two processes (d20). No pooled slope meta-analysis exists (d21); exact slopes still not confirmed.
agent_test: none (human finding)

claim: Response times alone cannot fix the format: Pylyshyn (tacit knowledge), Anderson (equivalence) and Intons-Peterson (experimenter expectation) show the same data can come from propositional codes or demand effects. The Jolicoeur-Kosslyn reply is cited from memory only. Gap-search: Intons-Peterson 1983 abstract read; expectations changed results in all four experiments. Jolicoeur-Kosslyn 1985 still has no readable abstract.
agent_test: none

claim: Neural evidence for a depictive format is mixed. Founding PET (Kosslyn 1995, baseline-dependent) and rTMS (Kosslyn 1999) support V1 involvement, V1 decoding exists even in aphantasia (Chang 2025). But a meta-analysis of 27 imagery fMRI experiments (380 subjects) found no early visual cortex activation, with Bayes factor under 0.33 (Spagna 2021), and attributes rTMS effects to spread. No pooled effect size for V1 exists.
agent_test: none

claim: Cortical blindness (patient SBR, VVIQ 1.9 vs controls 2.3) and aphantasia show imagery-like task performance can survive without V1 input or without reported experience, so experience, format and function can dissociate.
agent_test: none; samples small (1 patient; 61 vs 52 online)

claim: Aphantasia: object detail drops (0.261 vs 0.369 of objects drawn; OSIQ object scale d=3.80) while spatial layout is preserved (location error under 10% in both groups; OSIQ spatial scale t=-0.33, p=.742). Spatial and object-detail codes dissociate. Rotation tests stay at ceiling in Milton 2021.
agent_test: Test whether a layout-only (relational) summary versus an object-detail summary carries the task, per task type

claim: Vividness ratings and aphantasia labels are criterion-sensitive self-reports; group differences may be criterion confounds (2026 PBR argument, no new sample).
agent_test: none

claim: Asking an LLM to draw its state as a text grid after each step (VoT) beats plain CoT and no-viz for GPT-4. Re-checked in the paper: NL navigation 59.00 vs CoT 54.00 (only p<0.16) vs no-viz 35.50; tiling 63.94 vs 54.15; route planning completion 40.77 vs 37.02, success 14.72 vs 9.48. The gain over CoT is modest; it is large only over no-viz. Gap-search: no token-matched test found. A 2026 test of model-drawn ASCII before answering (Text2Space) gave no gain (d01).
agent_test: VoT-style state grid vs CoT at equal tokens on our spatial items; report against CoT, not only against no-viz

claim: A drawn state helps only when it is correct: state accuracy 26.48 and 24.25, compliance 51.14 and 52.01, correct decisions 65.16 and 77.20 when the drawing was accurate (paper Table 2). Gap-search: confirmed by a second study. Model-drawn ASCII accuracy was only 12-50%; draw-then-answer fell below text only in all base models (GPT-4.1 66.9 vs 71.7); answers consistent with the drawing were 89-97% accurate (d02). Drawing is the weak half (d14).
agent_test: Add a state-check step after each drawing and measure decision accuracy conditional on a correct drawing

claim: VoT is model- and task-dependent: little or no gain for GPT-3.5 and LLaMA3-8B, clear gain for LLaMA3-70B on some tasks, and a small loss on ring (modular arithmetic) navigation, CoT 52.5% vs VoT 49.5%. Gap-search: Whiteboard-of-Thought shows the same split by layout: square grid CoT 98 vs WoT 50, hexagon CoT 8 vs WoT 61 (GPT-4o).
agent_test: Route by task type: arithmetic or lookup to symbolic, spatial to grid; compare to always-grid

claim: Prompt wording moves state tracking: telling GPT-4 'use ascii-art to visualize' raised complete tracking to 98.5% (+78.5) and score to 62.5% (+3.5) on NL navigation; removing the word 'reasoning' from the VoT prompt lowered tracking (b24 had this wrong).
agent_test: Ablate the format instruction wording on our agent

claim: Text versus image of the same problem: models do worse with images. IsoBench gap 28.7 (Claude-3 Opus), 18.7 (GPT-4 Turbo), 14.9 (Gemini Pro) points on 1,887 samples. SpatialEval: text-only LLMs match or beat VLMs; removing or noising the image raised some VLMs (LLaVA-1.6-34B Spatial-Grid +20.1%; Maze-Nav noise image +6.5%). Gap-search: no 2025-26 re-run of IsoBench or SpatialEval found. On mazes in 2026, Claude Sonnet 4.6 scores 6% on images vs 80% on text grid, Opus 4.7 31% vs 90%. Part of image gaps comes from rendering and short outputs (d09).
agent_test: Same item as text and as rendered image at equal tokens; expect text to win on grids

claim: Remedies for the image deficit: translating the image to text first (IsoSP up to +14.4 on science) or combining both (IsoCB up to +9.4 on graph algorithms) recovers part of the gap.
agent_test: Always add a symbolic restatement beside any spatial form

claim: How a structure is written as text changes accuracy a lot: object-based ARC input nearly doubles GPT-4 solves on easy tasks (12-13 to 23 of 50), and graph encoding moves PaLM-62B from 19.8% to 53.8% on connected nodes.
agent_test: Compare raw grid, object list and coordinate list for the same puzzle at equal tokens

claim: Models solve spatial tasks that can be recoded as symbols and fail tasks needing real transformation: Cube Rolling 97.5-98.3% vs Mental Rotation 4.7-20.5% (human 100); rotation 56.7% vs human 79.6%; 3D rotation 50% vs human 79.16%; VisFactor best model 55.9% vs 78.8%.
agent_test: Send rotation-type subtasks to a tool (code, renderer), keep symbolic ones in text

claim: External imagery help alone is not enough: a rotating 3D renderer left GPT-5.2 at 50-62.5% (10 runs). Resetting to a canonical view gave 85-97.5% because it turns the task into 2D matching. Implied test set about 40 items. Only one study of this design; tools helped where objects can be cropped (o3 88.8% vs 47.8%). The minimum tool is a canonical-frame tool, not a renderer.
agent_test: Give the agent a tool that returns a canonical view; test rotation items

claim: In trained models, images as thoughts beat text where text coordinates fail: MVoT FrozenLake 85.60% vs CoT 61.48%; CoT falls .940 to .391 from 3x3 to 6x6 while MVoT stays .84-.89; 90.8% of CoT errors are wrong hole coordinates. CoT wins on Maze (about .98) when the layout is given as text.
agent_test: Test the analogous failure with coordinate text vs a grid on large boards
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Visual planning and latent visual tokens beat text only under training: VPRL 80.6 vs 53.6 SFT; FrozenLake 6x6 82.4 vs Gemini 2.5 Pro 38.8; Mirage gains are small (0.87 vs 0.84 CoT SFT on VSP; planning CoT 0.58 vs direct 0.76).
agent_test: none

claim: Text chain-of-thought can hurt spatial and perceptual tasks: VisFactor CoT hurt four tests, Mirage CoT SFT planning 0.47 vs direct SFT 0.72, Talk-like-a-Graph zero-cot below zero-shot, reasoning variants no better on blind-VLM tasks.
agent_test: At equal tokens compare direct vs CoT on spatial items; keep CoT off where it loses

claim: Letting the model draw with code and tools (Sketchpad) improves GPT-4o: math +11.2% avg, vision +14.3%, maxflow 25.0 to 66.3; humans draw the same auxiliary line 80% of the time. GPT-4 Turbo parity fell 80.5 to 71.5, so it is not uniform.
agent_test: Allow code-drawn diagrams as a tool; count cost per sample

claim: Asking the model to write a cognitive map first, then reason, lifts MindCube accuracy from 37.8% to 57.8% (+20.0).
agent_test: Map-then-reason prompt on our layout questions

claim: LLMs fail planning on text-described graphs (CogEval: GPT-4 0/30 shortest path one cluster away; 3-step 0.55); CoT and BFS/DFS hints helped only inconsistently.
agent_test: Offer a graph tool or explicit search instead of free-text navigation

claim: Reasoning models can pass an imagine-and-name task without pixels. Re-read in the paper: Gemini 3 Pro 3.65, GPT-5 3.35, o3-Pro 3.31, o3 3.13 vs human 2.85 (N=100, SD 1.51); Claude Opus 4.1 2.65 (p=.590) and o4-mini 2.66 not different from humans; Sonnet 4 poor; o3 with image generator 2.77. GPT-5 reasoning effort high 3.35 vs minimal 2.04. Still one preprint, no replication, items are symbolic shape assembly.
agent_test: Run Finke-Pinker-Farah style items on our agent with and without a drawn grid

claim: Text-only models encode some colour-space structure (Kendall tau .25-.33, 18 colour terms), weak support that perceptual structure needs no picture-like code.
agent_test: none

claim: VLM accuracy falls as human RT rises (r=-0.88 rotation, -0.73 Geoclidean, -0.97 numerosity), a serial-cost signature; correlational only.
agent_test: none

claim: Imagery of ambiguous figures resists reversal (Chambers & Reisberg) but construction tasks succeed (Finke, Pinker & Farah): images look interpreted, with the boundary at construction versus reinspection. Both recalled, not opened.
agent_test: none

claim: Models given a correct text grid beat the same models given an image of the same problem. MazeBench: Sonnet 4.6 6/100 on image vs 80/100 on text grid; Opus 4.7 31 vs 90; tokens per solve fall 4.4x and 5.8x. Even on images, frontier models first convert to a text grid and search in prose; a ban on that was ignored by Sonnet 4.6.
agent_test: Give the agent a verified text grid for grid mazes up to 20x20 and compare with a perceived image on tokens and accuracy

claim: A model-drawn grid before answering did not help in the only direct 2026 test. Text2Space: draw-then-answer GPT-4.1 66.9 vs text only 71.7; GPT-OSS-20B 83.8 vs 85.8; drawn grids were correct 12-50% of the time. A provided grid helped (GPT-4.1 75.3, both 78.4).
agent_test: Compare draw-first against plain CoT at equal tokens on a spatial item set; add a draw-vs-answer agreement check

claim: Draw-versus-answer agreement is a cheap trust signal: when the drawn ASCII and the text answer agreed, accuracy was 89-97% (Qwen3-235B 95.0, GPT-OSS-20B 97.0 on consistent cases), but only 46-76% of cases were consistent. Cost is one extra output.
agent_test: Use disagreement as a trigger to re-derive; log how often it fires and what it costs in tokens

claim: Task layout predicts when drawing beats text. Whiteboard-of-Thought (GPT-4o): text CoT wins on square grids (98 vs 50), drawing wins on hexagons (8 to 61) and visual ASCII art (0 to 92 on 3D). SpatialText and SiT-Bench: stated facts and global coordinates are easy; viewpoint change, rotation and cognitive mapping fail in text. No tested router rule exists yet.
agent_test: Hypothesis rule: standard text layout -> text state; frame change or irregular geometry -> recode to global coordinates or canonical view first. Test on mixed items

claim: Image input suppresses reasoning effort: 5-19x shorter outputs, and font alone swings accuracy up to 47 points; part of the text-vs-image gap is a rendering and prompt artifact, not perception. Text CoT alone does not rescue perceived spatial images (3% average loss across 17 models; GPT-5 +0.65 without CoT).
agent_test: When input is an image, require the same length of step-by-step output as in text mode and compare

claim: A model's own generated picture can be decorative. In unified multimodal models trained by plain SFT, dropping the thinking-image barely changed accuracy and a text CoT scored below no thinking; with a controlled same-teacher comparison, SVG thoughts beat text thoughts (MindCube 57.8 vs 42.5) once the model is trained to use them. Trained, not scaffold.
agent_test: Ask the agent to name the drawn cell or fact its answer relies on; drop the draw step if it is never cited

claim: Tool help in rotation tasks depends on what the tool returns. Perception tools help closed models on size and relation (Gemini-2.5-Pro +18.00 and +14.90 on two CVBench tasks) but a smaller model lost 8.06 on 3D distance. No study tested a plain code-execution tool for rotation by text-only agents.
agent_test: Test a code tool that rotates coordinate lists and returns a canonical form, against the same agent without it

claim: Meta-analytic human evidence is thin. Rotation meta-analyses pool sex differences (d = 0.60, 95% CI 0.54-0.67, 59 effects, 2026) and neural location (intraparietal sulcus, Zacks 2008), not RT slope. The one imagery fMRI meta-analysis (27 experiments, 380 subjects) found no early visual cortex activation (BF under 0.33).
agent_test: none

claim: Reasoning effort matters more than the picture for symbolic spatial assembly: GPT-5 on imagine-and-name moves 2.04 (minimal) to 3.35 (high) with reasoning effort, and an added image generator lowered o3 from 3.13 to 2.77. Claude Opus 4.1 (9000 thinking tokens) matched but did not beat humans.
agent_test: Run the same items on our agent at two thinking budgets with and without a drawn grid
